questions.text: What does activating an Agent Skill establish in the lifecycle taught by this lesson?

options.A: Its body has entered model-visible context; tool permissions and result verification remain separate.
options.B: Every executable helper in its directory has already run successfully.
options.C: All tools mentioned by the skill are automatically installed and authorized.
options.D: The host has verified that every artifact the skill will produce is correct.

questions.explanation: Activation loads instructions. Host-mediated execution, permission enforcement, and independent result verification are distinct later boundaries.

questions.text: A check must run every time a release event occurs; missing it is unacceptable. Which primitive best fits that requirement?

options.A: A skill selected implicitly from its description.
options.B: A prompt the user may choose to paste.
options.C: A reference document loaded only when the agent judges it relevant.
options.D: A deterministic hook or application code triggered by the event.

questions.explanation: Mandatory event-driven execution belongs in hooks or application code, rather than probabilistic model selection.

questions.text: In select_primitives, each flag is checked with a separate if. TaskShape has repeatable_method=True and external_capability=True, with every other flag False. What does it return?

options.A: ("Agent Skill",), because the first match ends selection.
options.B: ("Agent Skill", "MCP tool"), because both responsibilities are selected.
options.C: ("MCP tool",), because external capability overrides procedure.
options.D: ("prompt",), because multiple matching flags are ambiguous.

questions.explanation: The independent if statements append both selections in order. The prompt fallback applies only when choices is empty.
